Action Plan:
1. Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler ‒ dose/route/frequency not documented; to be used PRN for wheeze.  
2. Prescribe Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler ‒ dose/route/frequency not documented; to be used regularly as controller therapy once symptoms settle.  
3. Prescribe a 5-day course of oral corticosteroids (two tablets each morning; exact drug/dose not documented).  
4. Supply a spacer device with written instructions for correct inhaler technique.  
5. Safety-net advice: if Salbutamol is needed more often than every 3 hours, or if chest tightness/shortness of breath worsens, seek urgent medical review (GP, urgent care, or ED).  
6. Advise relative rest and allow self-certified sick leave for up to 7 days; formal fit note if symptoms persist.  
7. Educate regarding potential steroid side-effects (mood change, hyperglycaemia, rash, nausea, headache) and advise reading pharmacy information leaflet.  
8. Arrange electronic transmission of prescriptions within the hour to local pharmacy.  
9. No further investigations arranged; consider peak-flow monitoring in future reviews.  
10. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 3-hour history of chest tightness.  
• HPI: Tight chest with mild shortness of breath (worse on stairs, not at rest), wheeze, non-productive cough. Recent “cold” over past week with sore throat & runny nose now improving; cough persists. No chest pain, haemoptysis, fever, or sputum.  
• Past medical history: Asthma (severe exacerbation requiring intubation age 16-17), allergic rhinitis/hay fever, childhood eczema, childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).  
• Past surgical history: None mentioned.  
• Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (out of supply for 1 week), Beclomethasone inhaler (out of supply for 1 week).  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies; environmental allergy to dust.  
• Family history: Father ‒ asthma; Mother ‒ eczema.  
• Social history: 26-year-old university student. Smoking/alcohol status not documented.

Objective:
• Remote consultation ‒ no physical examination performed.  
• Patient able to speak full sentences; not short of breath at rest.  
• No vitals, peak flow, or imaging available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Issue: Acute asthma exacerbation  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation (DDx item: “Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by viral URI and lapse in controller therapy” – High likelihood).  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways (DDx – Medium) – supporting: recent cold; opposing: underlying asthma/non-adherence.  
     • Community-acquired pneumonia (DDx – Low) – opposing: no fever, sputum, pleuritic pain.  
     • Pulmonary embolism (DDx – Low) – opposing: no risk factors, pain, tachypnoea.  
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; consider peak-flow measurement at follow-up.  
   - Treatment planned:  
     • Salbutamol inhaler PRN.  
     • Beclomethasone inhaler regular use once recovered.  
     • 5-day course oral corticosteroids (two tablets AM, drug/dose not documented).  
     • Spacer device.  
     • Education on inhaler technique and steroid side-effects.  
     • Safety-netting as above.  
   - Relevant referrals: None today; urgent care/ED if deterioration.

2. Issue: Work/academic fitness  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Need for short-term sick leave due to asthma exacerbation.  
   - Investigations planned: None.  
   - Treatment/Management: Advise rest; patient may self-certify first 7 days; formal fit note if needed.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Vitals (HR, RR, BP, SpO₂, temperature), objective respiratory examination, smoking history, alcohol use, vaccination status, detailed dosing instructions for prescribed medications.  
• Internal conflicts: None detected between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; brief audio dropout noted but context preserved.
